name: USGS 1998 EM300 original 5 m Monterey Canyon–Point Sur grids

producer.name: U.S. Geological Survey; 1998 EM300 survey A4-98-MB

units.bathymetry_elevation: m; vertical datum unspecified in the original metadata

spatial.horizontal_crs: NAD83 UTM zone 10N; original ArcInfo grids read as EPSG:26910

temporal.update_cadence: Static historical grid; monthly byte-integrity and research-overlap review

provenance.access_service: Official USGS Open-File Report 01-179 ArcInfo-grid file directory
transformations: Downloaded and SHA-256 pinned the complete MTSHLF5G and SGF5G ArcInfo grid members plus original metadata; original bytes stay in ignored research storage.
Masked populated 5 m cells under 17 generalized research outlines and paired their centers with the later original USGS 2 m depth grid; published aggregate counts and elevation differences only.
Kept all datum, uncertainty, independence, navigation and fishing release gates false.

evidence.supports: Official survey year, NAD83 UTM 10, four 5 m grid extents, original processing notes and research/navigation limitations.

Official downloadable original SGF5G grid with 972 valid 5 m cells in the formerly uncovered historical-camera research outline 001; none is nominally 200–300 ft in the source's undocumented vertical datum.
Official downloadable original MTSHLF5G grid with populated research overlap north of SGF5G and a source comparison at outline 040.

limitations: The original metadata do not declare a vertical datum or an upper vertical-error bound; native depths cannot qualify the 300 ft MLLW limit.
The later 2016 USGS composite may incorporate the same survey. Paired differences are not independent validation or total propagated uncertainty.
Only two of the four original EM300 grids were acquired because their published footprints touch the reviewed Monterey outlines; this is not a whole-coast survey inventory.

Historical camera windows and interpreted hard-bottom outlines do not establish a current catch site. The newly covered camera outline 001 already intersects bounded official MPA and ENC danger review layers; current rules and complete drift routes remain separate gates.
The source explicitly says it is not intended for navigation, and product-specific redistribution terms have not been reviewed.
